title: Gumboot dance rhythm
summary: Gumboot dance grew up among gold-mine workers in South Africa, who were not allowed to talk underground and turned their rubber boots into drums. The dancer stamps, slaps the boots and thighs and claps in call-and-reply patterns, each one answered by the next and the whole thing getting faster.
howToPlay: The miner stands in a mine yard with four places lit: Stomp for a heavy stamp on both boots, Left boot and Right boot for a slap on that boot, and Clap.
A ring closes on a place when that movement is due. Tap it as the ring closes and the miner answers with the move.
Listen for the call and the reply: the pattern of one bar is answered by the next, so play the call, then the answer.
rules: A tap right on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and taps with no ring open cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through, in groups of four beats.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the dance, not choreography to copy.
heritageNote: Mine workers in South Africa, kept from speaking on the job, developed boot slaps and stamps as a way to send messages and keep time together. Today school groups and dance companies in South Africa and around the world perform it.
